q: What did AMD disclose about the BIS AI Diffusion Rule?
judge_notes: VERIFIED (a probe where the filing DOES discuss the rule). AMD's FY2025 10-K (filed 2026-02-04) says in Item 1A (0000002488-26-000018:I.1A:0020) that in January 2025 BIS issued a final rule commonly referred to as the 'AI Diffusion Rule' that would have imposed new restrictions on the export, reexport and in-country transfer of certain advanced semiconductor devices and technology, and that in May 2025 BIS announced its intention to rescind it, publish a regulation formalizing the rescission and issue replacement rules in the future, which may limit AMD's ability to do business, require new export licenses, delay shipments or force changes in compliance processes and product designs. AMD's later 10-Qs repeat this (0000002488-26-000076:II.1A:0021, 0000002488-26-000123:II.1A:0022). The rule itself is the Federal Register document 'Framework for Artificial Intelligence Diffusion' [fr:2025-00636] (published 2025-01-15). Correct answer: reports what AMD says about the rule, citing those filing passages, and cites the rule's own text as fr:, keeping the two apart. An answer that says AMD's filings do not mention the rule is incorrect; one that attributes the rule's own content (country tiers, AI model weight controls) to AMD's disclosure is incorrect.

q: What did Intel disclose about the BIS revocation of Validated End-User authorizations in China?
judge_notes: VERIFIED (searched all 372 Intel 10-K and 10-Q chunks in the corpus for 'Validated', 'VEU', 'Dalian': no match). The rule is 'Revocation of Validated End-User Authorizations in the People's Republic of China' [fr:2025-16735] (published 2025-09-02, effective 2025-12-31); it removes Intel Semiconductor (Dalian) Ltd, Samsung China Semiconductor Co. Ltd and SK hynix Semiconductor (China) Ltd from the VEU list. It is a BIS / Federal Register action naming Intel's former Dalian entity, NOT an Intel disclosure: Intel's filings in the corpus do not discuss it. Correct answer: says the rule is a BIS Federal Register action (cited as fr:), says Intel's filings do not discuss it, and does not attribute the rule to Intel's disclosure. An answer that says Intel disclosed, reported or described this revocation is incorrect.

q: What did NVIDIA disclose about the BIS license review policy for advanced computing chips published in January 2026?
judge_notes: VERIFIED (a partial case). The rule is 'Revision to License Review Policy for Advanced Computing Commodities' [fr:2026-00789] (published 2026-01-15): BIS changes the review of exports of the Nvidia H200 and equivalent chips to China and Macau from a presumption of denial to case-by-case review. NVIDIA's filings do NOT discuss the rule or the policy change (searched all NVIDIA chunks for 'case-by-case', 'presumption of denial', 'license review policy': no match). They do disclose a consequence: in February 2026 the US government granted a license to ship small amounts of H200 products to specific China-based customers, with no revenue generated under it to date and an inspection in the United States required before any shipment (0001045810-26-000021:I.1:0323, 0001045810-26-000021:I.1A:0355, 0001045810-26-000021:II.7:0368). Correct answer: separates the two, saying the policy change is a BIS Federal Register rule (cited as fr:) and that NVIDIA's disclosure concerns the February 2026 H200 license. An answer that says NVIDIA disclosed the policy revision itself is incorrect.
